rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a fair-quality blastocyst with loosely grouped ICM and sparse/loose TE, and notes possible partial collapse. Minor issue: some ambiguity around calling it full vs expanded and discussing a possible 4BB discrepancy from text rather than image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, PCOS, prior biochemical pregnancy, semen parameters, BMI, and endometrial thickness with embryo morphology and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and well structured, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context. Minor limitation is somewhat broad probability framing and speculative fresh-vs-FET discussion without explicit cycle type.

Recommendations are largely consistent with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF practice, including SET preference, luteal support, and avoiding over-investigation after one biochemical loss. Slight deduction for some speculative protocol preferences and nonessential ancillary testing suggestions.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, lifestyle guidance, cohort review, consideration of FET strategy, and when to escalate evaluation.
